body: My biggest battle is the starting position — keeping the back straight, chest open, elbows out and lats engaged before the bar leaves the floor. When I lose it there, everything downstream suffers: the hips rise first in the pull and I end up doing the work with my arms. In the turnover the recurring miss is elbows not going to the sky, which opens space between me and the bar. Staying over the bar longer has been helping the hips, and the first full snatches (35–37kg) felt genuinely good — but the receiving position is still inconsistent: sometimes wobbly overhead, sometimes not caught deep enough, sometimes the bar drifts back and I can't stabilise it.

The dip and drive is where I struggle most — I drift forward of vertical, and it gets worse as the bar gets heavier. "Head to the ceiling" has helped a lot. Above ~50kg the drive loses aggression and the misses show up: press-outs, catching forward, and a split where the back leg still isn't planted. Re-racking between jerks is a skill I'm still learning — if my hips are open, the bar pushes me backwards. The clean itself is the part that feels best (I really like cleans) and the pulls feel stronger with the back more engaged lately, though at heavier weights the elbows still don't turn over fast enough and my lats let go.
